title: Survey Reveals Power of Personality in Getting Hired
paragraphs: Experience and skill are both really important when applying for a job — but personality may be just as important!
In fact, in a survey of US hiring managers, 91% said that personality matters as much as skill. And for 86%, an applicant's personality can even make up for missing skills.
The survey was done by research company The Harris Poll for Express Employment Professionals, and included 1,000 hiring decision-makers at US businesses.
It found that hiring managers often rely on moments that take place outside of prepared interview questions to decide if a candidate's personality will fit their company's culture.
These might include small talk before or after the interview, the tone of the candidate's emails, and how they interact with other office staff.
First impressions really count too, as 87% of hiring managers agree they can tell from the very first conversation if a candidate will succeed at their company.
The biggest personality traits hiring managers say they value include reliability, honesty, adaptability, flexibility and self-motivation.
And having the right personality doesn't just help you get the job. According to 99% of hiring managers, a positive personality plays an important role in advancing your career.
Job candidates know how important personality is too. In a similar survey of 1,000 US job seekers by the same researchers, 61% said they worry about how their personality comes across in interviews.

Nearly all job seekers — 94% — said companies looked at their personalities while they were being interviewed for a job, either through informal interactions, questions about how they'd act in certain situations, or personality tests.

So if you want to do well in an interview, you don't just have to show that you have the necessary skills for the job — you also need to show that you're reliable, honest, adaptable, flexible and motivated!
